findings.title: A cancelled online order paid into a drawer that closed before the cancel: the hand-back books a fake 1110 receivable and leaves 1010 negative
findings.scenario: Reproduced in scratchpad/rv/voidThenCancel.rv.test.ts (DB servd_test_money_rv). Steps: a storefront takeout order (source servd, 11,500) has its cash paid into drawer A while it is still open. A closes, and because the order is not cancelled yet the close books it as non-till cash: Dr 1015 / Cr 1010 11,500. The order is then cancelled. refundOrder goes to refundDueOnCancelledTicket, refundDueCents is 11,500, and the refund is accepted. In postRefundPayment, saleBookingOf returns booked=false (no order.complete, and no home drawer for a non-pos order) and refundDue=false (no 1110 line, because the close did not treat it as cancelled). onDrawer is true, so it books Dr 1110 / Cr 1015. Result: 1110 is left with a debit of 11,500 (a receivable from nobody), 1010 is left with a credit of 11,500, and 1015 nets to zero. The builder's 'nets 1110 to zero' claim only covers a cancel that happens before the receiving drawer closes.
findings.fix: In the cancelled / rejected branch, find out where each receipt was parked. Drawer still open: Dr 1110 is correct, because that close will see the order as cancelled. Drawer closed with a refund-due line: Dr 1110. Drawer closed before the cancel, for a non-pos order (non-till cash, Dr 1015 / Cr 1010): debit 1010 (CASH_ON_HAND), not 1110. Alternatively, have cancelOrder reclass 1010 to 1110 for those receipts. Add a test where the drawer closes before the cancel.

findings.title: A refund taken while the order was still open (TILL-R3 void) and then a cancel leaves 1110 credited and negative revenue and GST on a ticket that was never sold
findings.file: /home/user/servd/backend/src/modules/accounting/shiftPosting.ts (summariseShiftSales cancelledPaid / refund-due line), together with /home/user/servd/backend/src/modules/pos/service.ts refundDueOf
findings.scenario: Reproduced in scratchpad/rv/voidThenCancel.rv.test.ts. Steps: an order (11,500 incl. 1,500 GST) takes 11,500 cash on drawer S1 while still open. An item is voided and refunded as a TILL-R3 refund row of 2,300. postRefundPayment books it as a sale refund (Dr 4090 2,000 / Dr 2030 300 / Cr 1015 2,300), because the order is not cancelled yet. The order is then cancelled. refundDueCents correctly gives 9,200, and refundDueOnCancelledTicket hands back 9,200 (Dr 1110 / Cr 1015). S1 closes, and the close credits 1110 for the GROSS receipts of 11,500, not net of the refund already handed back. End state: 1110 is credited 2,300 (a liability nobody is owed), revenue is debited 2,000 and output tax 300 for a sale that was never booked or filed. The customer amount is right, but the ledger is not.
findings.fix: For a never-sold order, the close's refund-due line should be its receipts less refunds already handed back on it. Any earlier refund booked as a sale refund also needs its revenue and tax shares reversed (Cr 4xxx / Cr 203x, Dr 1110), either at the cancel or at the close. Alternatively, have cancelOrder reclass existing 'order.refund' entries of the order into Dr 1110 / Cr revenue and tax. Add the void-then-cancel case to auditMoneyFollowups.

findings.title: A cancel after the drawer already booked the sale, then a full hand-back, leaves revenue, GST and a 1110 receivable on a cancelled order (the ledger disagrees with the register)
findings.scenario: Reproduced in scratchpad/rv/voidThenCancel.rv.test.ts. Steps: a till dine-in bill of 11,500 (1,500 GST) is part-paid 5,000 cash on S1. S1 closes, booking the sale: Cr 4090 10,000, Cr 2030 1,500, Dr 1015 5,000, Dr 1110 6,500 unsettled. The order is cancelled, and refundOrder hands back 5,000 through refundDueOnCancelledTicket. saleBookingOf returns booked=true, so postRefundPayment books a pro-rata sale refund (Dr 4090 4,348 / Dr 2030 652 / Cr 1015). Because the new path keeps the order 'cancelled' and skips postOrderRefund, nothing reverses the rest. End state: revenue 5,652 and output GST 848 stay on the books, with a Dr 1110 receivable of 6,500 against a cancelled order whose money has all been handed back. The sales register leaves cancelled orders out, so it shows 0 while the P&L shows 5,652.
findings.fix: When a cancelled order's sale is already booked (booking.booked), either refuse the hand-back until the booked sale is reversed, or have the cancel post a reversal of the booked sale (Dr revenue / tax, Cr 1110 for the unsettled part, Cr 1110 refund due for the money taken) so the hand-back then takes the refund-due branch. Cover this with a test where the drawer closes before the cancel.

findings.title: The sales register adds gift cards back for sales booked before ONL-05 (legacy), so its gross, net and GST disagree with the P&L for those orders
findings.scenario: ONL-05 (the 2080 debit and the pre-card revenue) is uncommitted, and no backfill script exists in backend/scripts. So every gift-card sale already on the production books is a 'legacy' booking: revenue was taken on the post-card total, with no 2080 line. The ledger's refunds handle these through asBooked(legacyGiftCard): they value the order without the card, and the card restore books nothing. salesBuckets now always adds every redemption to gross and values refunds and card restores including the card. Example: a legacy 1,150 order with a 500 card. The P&L net is 500 (650 − 150 GST); the register shows 1,000. After a refund, the GST shares also differ, so the register stops matching /accounting/pl-ledger for any period containing those orders.
findings.fix: Skip the add-back for orders whose sale has no 2080 debit naming the order (the same check as saleBookingOf.legacyGiftCard). Alternatively, ship a one-off backfill that books the 2080 or revenue reclass for legacy gift-card sales before deploy, so every sale is valued pre-card.
